date_note: Cumhuriyet (21 November) reports AEK's announcement but gives no earlier day for the attack; the article's publication day is used.
exec: A major football club says its official website was attacked ahead of a high-profile match; the club blames Turkish hackers.
geo_basis: club home ground named in the source (AEK Arena), Athens
impact: AEK's official website was attacked, according to the club as reported by Cumhuriyet; the article gives no detail on disruption or data.
plain: The Greek football club AEK said its official website was hit by a cyberattack before its Champions League match against Galatasaray. The club said Turkish hackers were behind it, Turkish newspaper Cumhuriyet reports.
summary: Cumhuriyet reports that the Greek football club AEK announced a cyberattack on its official website ahead of its Champions League match against Galatasaray. According to the article, AEK alleged the attack was carried out by Turkish hackers and called it a cowardly attack with provocative and ultra-nationalist content. The article does not say when the attack happened or what effect it had.
title: Greek club AEK says its official website was hit by a cyberattack before Galatasaray match, blames Turkish hackers

validation.note: Single publisher read (Cumhuriyet), which relays AEK's statement; AEK's own statement was not read. Onedio reports the same but its article body did not load. Attribution to Turkish hackers is AEK's claim only.
